When implementation **empirically refutes** an active criterion (e.g. the dispatching brief says "all 16 files" but measurement finds 12), the criterion can stop governing ONLY through the evidence-preserving amendment path — never by silent deletion or by "satisfying" a falsified requirement.%0A+%0A+ Per story, `acceptanceCriteria` holds the currently governing criteria, and the optional `criterionAmendments` ledger retains every refuted original verbatim:%0A+%0A+ ```jsonc%0A+ {%0A+   "kind": "replaced", // or "superseded" (no replacement governs)%0A+   "original": "All 16 files that set FDFT_WHALE_STREAM=1 are classified affected/not-affected WITH EVIDENCE",%0A+   "replacement": "All 12 files that set FDFT_WHALE_STREAM=1 are classified affected/not-affected WITH EVIDENCE",%0A+   "reason": "The brief count was wrong: 7 listed names are readers/asserters/doc-recipes, not setters",%0A+   "evidence": "Enumerated setters via grep FDFT_WHALE_STREAM=1: 12 setters, 16 total matches",%0A+   "authority": "ses_<ralph-session-id>",%0A+   "timestamp": "2026-08-10T03:15:00.000Z"%0A+ }%0A+ ```%0A+%0A+ Programmatic API (from `src/hooks/ralph`): `amendCriterion(dir, storyId, { original, replacement, reason, evidence, authority })` replaces an active criterion and inserts the corrected one at its position; `supersedeCriterion(dir, storyId, { original, reason, evidence, authority })` removes it with no replacement. Both require non-empty reason/authority and bounded evidence (`MIN_CRITERION_EVIDENCE_LENGTH = 10`); failures return closed error codes and never mutate the PRD.%0A+%0A+ Fail-closed invariants: a malformed ledger entry, an amended original that is still active, or an original amended twice makes the PRD invalid on read (`readPrd` → `null`), matching existing invalid-PRD startup behavior. Legacy PRDs without `criterionAmendments` still read and format normally, but a completion or architect-verification claim lacking its governing-criteria revision is reopened and requires current-criteria re-verification before it can progress. An empty `[]` ledger is treated as absent. Older builds that rewrite a PRD serialize only fields their own normalizer knows, so amendment records are only preserved by builds that ship this schema.
